about: The one map of BYT. It says what a tap means (bins, axes, styles, faculties), where it leads (skills), who takes part (seats), how value moves (incomes), which AI agents work between the seats and what each may touch (agents), and the numbers every rule runs on (rules). Code reads the content parts from this file, and a test checks the agents and the rule numbers against the code. Anyone publishing a gate, a skill, a job or a question uses these ids, or adds to this file first: the server refuses to start on a tag or id it does not know. The brain regions are loose textbook associations. Nothing here measures a brain.

bins.name: Preference
bins.about: Pick one. There is no wrong answer.

bins.name: Games
bins.about: Find the one move that wins.

bins.name: Skills
bins.about: Each one has a right answer. They get harder.

bins.name: Twin battles
bins.about: Your twin guesses your picks first.

styles.name: Analyze
styles.about: You look for proof first. You ask what is true and what the numbers say.
styles.strength: You find the mistake in a plan before it costs anything.
styles.watch: Waiting too long to be sure, and forgetting how a choice feels to other people.

styles.name: Organize
styles.about: You turn a goal into steps. Then you finish the steps.
styles.strength: You finish what you start, and you finish on time.
styles.watch: Keeping the old plan after the facts have changed.

styles.name: Explore
styles.about: You look for the choice that no one listed. You see how different things connect.
styles.strength: You see what something could become before there is proof.
styles.watch: Starting more things than you finish.

styles.name: Connect
styles.about: You notice how people feel, and you choose with people in mind.
styles.strength: People follow you because they feel heard.
styles.watch: Making a message so gentle that it no longer says what it must say.

faculties.name: Planning and self-control
faculties.about: You keep a goal in mind. You wait for the better choice. You think one step ahead.
faculties.fact: This part of the brain is one of the last to finish growing. It keeps growing after age 20.

faculties.name: Working things out
faculties.about: You start from what you know, and you work toward what must be true.
faculties.fact: Your mind can hold only about 4 things at one time. Writing a problem down helps you think.

faculties.name: Wanting new things
faculties.about: You feel a pull toward what is new, what is bold, or what is a treat.
faculties.fact: A brain chemical called dopamine is strongest when a reward is better than you expected. Surprise is the signal.

faculties.name: Understanding people
faculties.about: You work out what another person thinks, feels and wants.
faculties.fact: By about age 4, most children understand that another person can believe something that is not true.

faculties.name: Imagination
faculties.about: You picture things that are not in front of you, like the future or a different choice.
faculties.fact: This network is most active when you are not doing a task, for example when you daydream or remember.

faculties.name: Habits
faculties.about: You stay with what has worked, and you like what you know well.
faculties.fact: When something becomes a habit, the brain does it with very little effort. That is why habits are easy to keep and hard to stop.

faculties.name: Reaction speed
faculties.about: How fast you move after you see a signal.
faculties.fact: A healthy adult needs about a quarter of a second to react to something they see.

skills.name: Strategy
skills.about: Find the winning move. Then find it faster.

skills.name: Logic
skills.about: Finish the pattern. Find what must be true.

skills.name: Planning
skills.about: Put the steps in the best order.

skills.name: New ideas
skills.about: Find more choices, and better ones.

skills.name: Understanding people
skills.about: Guess what another person will pick, and why.

skills.name: Your voice
skills.about: Say it the way you would say it.

seats.name: Player
seats.gives: Taps, and a yes or no on the twin's work
seats.gets: A twin, certificates, work income, data income
seats.sees: Everything stored about them, on screen
seats.never_sees: Another player's answers, beliefs or nickname

seats.name: Agency
seats.gives: Play credits for each twin that answers
seats.gets: Counts for each answer across the twins that match
seats.sees: Totals over 5 or more twins. One twin's nickname and answers only when that twin's owner turned one to one on and the agency paid the royalty
seats.never_sees: A twin whose owner did not turn one to one on; which twin said what in a group
seats.sphere: One tight cluster of points for each group of twins it could reach (grouped by strongest thinking style), one for twins still forming, one for other agencies, one for creators. A group turns gold once the agency has asked it.

seats.name: Creator
seats.gives: Play credits for each twin its crew asks; a fee to claim a skill step and a crew fee to build it
seats.gets: Counts for a survey or a test across a group; a skill step it claims and builds by tapping cards from a pack; a royalty from the growth fund each time another player passes that step
seats.sees: Totals over 5 or more twins. One twin's nickname and answers only when that twin's owner turned one to one on and the creator paid the royalty
seats.never_sees: A twin whose owner did not turn one to one on; one player's progress
seats.sphere: One tight cluster for each group of players, grouped by the thinking style they most need to grow, plus other creators and agencies.

incomes.name: Work income
incomes.who_answers: The Worker agent (AI), or the practice twin when AI is not available
incomes.human_check: Always. Nothing is paid or counted until the player says the answer is right or corrects it
incomes.paid_by: The agency that posted the job, from credits it put on hold. The three starter jobs have made-up requesters

incomes.name: Data income
incomes.who_answers: Plain code from the player's pick counts. No AI, no tokens
incomes.human_check: None per question. The player turns the whole stream on or off; it is off until they turn it on

incomes.name: Growth bonus
incomes.who_answers: No one. It is paid when a player passes a skill step
incomes.human_check: None needed. Code checks the step was passed
incomes.paid_by: The growth fund, which is filled by the extra that agencies pay for asking the same group again

incomes.name: One to one royalty
incomes.who_answers: Plain code from the player's pick counts. No AI, no tokens
incomes.human_check: None per meeting. The player turns one to one on or off; it is off until they turn it on
incomes.paid_by: The agency or creator that meets the twin

agents.job: Reads a player's picks and writes short beliefs about them
agents.reads: The player's own picks that are not held back for a battle, and reviewed job answers
agents.never_reads: Nickname, token, player id, held-back picks, what the player told the twin, any other player
agents.output: Up to 8 beliefs, each with the number of picks behind it
agents.checked_by: Prompt guard, length cap; then stored by code and shown to the player

agents.job: Guesses the player's picks on cards the player has not seen
agents.reads: The beliefs and the cards to guess, without trait tags
agents.never_reads: Nickname, token, player id, the raw picks, the right answers, any other player
agents.output: One guess for each card, or no guess
agents.checked_by: Each guess must be a real option of a real card; scored by code against the real picks

agents.job: Answers one job question as the player would, with a one-line reason
agents.reads: The beliefs and one question with its options, without trait tags
agents.never_reads: Nickname, token, player id, the requester's name, any other player
agents.output: One option, or no answer, and a reason of one sentence
agents.checked_by: The option must exist; the reason passes the prompt guard; then the player approves or corrects it

agents.job: Answers one line the player said to their twin, and offers one move
agents.reads: The beliefs, the player's progress and open work as counts, the list of moves, and the one line the player said
agents.never_reads: Nickname, token, player id, any other player, anything the player said before
agents.output: One or two sentences and at most one move
agents.checked_by: The line passes the prompt guard before the run; the answer passes it after; the move must be on the list code gave; the line is not stored

Cards touching an area that fill its slice of the sphere

Play credits the growth fund starts with, so the first skill steps can be rewarded
Paid from the growth fund when a player passes a skill step
Connections with others at which a twin shows its full color
The days looked at when the game says how often a player played
Played within this many days: the twin receives its full share of data income
Played within this many days: half. Longer ago: a quarter
What a creator pays each twin its crew asks in a group
What a seat pays the game each time its crew goes out. The crew is plain code, so this is a flat fee, not a token fee
What a creator pays the game to claim a waiting skill step
The royalty for meeting one twin one to one. Large on purpose: seeing who a twin is costs far more than asking a group
Fixed pay for one checked answer to a job an agency posts, so no typed amount. Far more than a group question, because the Worker agent answers and the owner checks it
How many twins may take a posted job. Never fewer than 5

Fixed amounts an agency may put behind a skill, so no typed amount
What a sponsorship pays the player and the creator each time a built step of that skill is passed

Cards a creator taps from a pack to build a skill step. Three of four right passes it

principles.rule: The size and weight of a point come from progress and from how many people it stands for, never from credits held or spent.
principles.where: main.seat_groups: a point's size is the twin's progress

principles.rule: An agency is charged the same price for every twin in a group. A twin's share of that price depends only on how lately its owner played, never on money. A group cannot be bought by one large payer.
Each agency sees a balance score: how evenly it has reached across the groups. Reaching only one group scores low.
What raises a twin's pay is proof of progress (a certificate), which is earned by play and checked by code.
A seat can look at a group of 5 or more, never at one person. A smaller group is hidden.
When an agency asks the same group again, the price rises each time. The twins are still paid the same; the extra goes to the growth fund.
The growth fund pays a bonus to a player who passes a skill step, and a smaller royalty to the creator who built that step. The player is paid first. The fund can only pay what it holds.
A twin that has only played alone is black and white. Color comes from connecting with others: work checked, questions answered, the choice to earn. Groups of people are always in color.

The game keeps one row for each day a player used it. Agencies and creators see how many twins in a group played lately, as a count. A twin whose owner has not played lately receives less data income, and the part held back goes to the growth fund.
